questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Good academic program as well as a nice living area with good opportunities to explore during my time off

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The information is given to you along the way, but it can't be a bit stressfull for a person (like me) who likes to have all the information at once and in early in the proces... But otherwise, you get an email where you can ask all the questions you might have, so you will always be able to find it somehow.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The host university arranged a "welcome day" where they gave a lot of information that the international students needed for our stay. Otherwise, they just provided us with the information on where we could get help for all the inquiries we may have during our exchange.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: My uni provided some places for student accommodations since they didn't have housing opportunities at campus. Nevertheless, most of these student accommodations have a 6 months policy, which means that you have to live there for at least six months :/ And the few that don't have these policy, you just need to apply some months in advance so you are sure you get an apartment in the period you want

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Nothing really... Just make sure that your place isn't too far away from the campus - a good thumb-rule is max 30 min travel-distance from your place to campus

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You registered all your classes from home, some weeks before the semester starts. The only thing that annoyed me was, that some courses (like courses involved in some aspects of psychology) are harder to get, if they can't see the necessary requirements or something like that. But you always have the option to switch courses when you arrive and then you can get help from the administration of the host university, which sometimes makes it easier to get the courses you want

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Different administrations or help-centers at the school where available every day for these kinds of inquires

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: in first round of applying I got 3 out of 4 classes that I wanted. I later switched to the last class I wanted with help from muy host uni

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Always pick a few extra courses, so you are sure that you will get 4 courses. Then later you can switch them out if there were some of the courses you didn't want after all

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The levels of my courses ranged from level 1-3

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: A bit different. Still have the same system with lectures and tutorials like at UCPH, but at my host uni we had way more assignments during the semester than I usually have at UCPH, since the grading system is different at my host uni.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Musculoskeletal, Neurological and Occupational Disorders 
Food and Nutrition
Sport Psychology
Cell Biology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Can't really recommend any specific courses, since it depends on what you wanna focus on and what topics you find interesting... I found all of my courses very interesting in different ways, but if I could undo one thing, it would be to switch out the first cours with something else, since it was super tough and not really that applicable to my study (this was more for a specific job-position that we don't really have in Denmark).

questions.question: Insurance DKK *
Housing DKK per month *
Books DKK per month *
Local transportation DKK per month *
Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *
Communication (phone, internet, etc.) DKK per month *
Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Visa, travel inquiries (while I was abroad and wanted to travel to other countries nearby) and a lot of small expenses on random stuff for my room

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing was almost twice as expensive as back home in Denmark :( But food (mostly fruit and veggies) from grocery stores or local markeds were usually a bit cheaper compared to back home.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were some parties arranges in the beginning that you could attend for a specific amount. Otherwise, my host uni had tons of social clubs you could be a part of - I joined the surf club as many other international students, and went on one surf trip.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Depending on your interest to be honest. I liked the surf club  - just because I always wanted to try it. I met so many sweet people on my surf trip, but unfortunately they get sold out pretty fast and can be a bit expensive, but still nice to just go on one, so you can try to surf and meet new people!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I was in Brisbane, Australia and I loved it. A lot of people went on roadtrips to nearby cities during the weekends or holidays. A lot of my friends did most of the east coast during their mid semester break (1 week long). I went to Fiji during the break. But the opportunities are endless. So many things to do and see around there.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. The same as back home - just needed to get used to them driving in the left side of the road instead of the right

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I only had classes with local students, so for me it was easy to meet them. They can be a bit hard to socialize with, since they won't really approach you even when they know you are an exchange student (they know you are leaving soon so they don't wanna bother). But I still got some friends in each class, you just have to be the first to approach

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Mostly the group work, since they don't really do it as much here as back in UCPH. The group work mostly consisted in delegating the different parts to every group member and then meet up once or twice before you had to hand it in/do the presentation....

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I don't think that I appreciated something in particular, but I liked that there was a lot of study spots outside, where you could charge your electronically device! Also, the campus had a lot of different cafes, so you could always get some good study snacks or a nice little coffee break when needed!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Buy an adapter
- If you need some books for your semester, then look them up in the library first - I found all mine there and therefore didn't have to pay anything
- Socialize and really try to participate in the events they have in the beginning - that's where you will meet a lot of new people and usually also there where you will find your group

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: people in the HiQ center is always helpfull and can answer most of your questions

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting new friends and really evolve my English skills (both oral and in writing)

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: mostly how there school system work with and how they aspect to make the different assignments, since they had some different rules or standards for this compared to back home

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
